Getting started

bots is one dependency-free ES module that draws plush, animated avatars for AI agents and apps. This page gets one on screen and wired to your agent in about five minutes.

Install#

From GitHub, for projects with a bundler. The release branch holds the built package, updated on every change to main:

npm i github:kucukkanat/bots#release

Import it as @kucukkanat/bots (and /react, /vue, /svelte, /export, /packs/…). To pin a version, use a commit of that branch: github:kucukkanat/bots#<commit>.

Or straight from a CDN, with no build step at all. The module registers the <bot-avatar> element as soon as it loads:

<script type="module" src="https://kucukkanat.github.io/bots/dist/bots.js"></script>

Self-hosting? Copy the src/ folder anywhere your site serves static files. The renderer starts its worker threads from that folder, so keep the files together.

Your first bot#

Drop the element anywhere. Every option is an attribute in kebab-case; change one and the avatar eases into its new look.

<bot-avatar type="clover" size="96"></bot-avatar>
<bot-avatar type="cat" face="mouth" hat="party" bow-tie></bot-avatar>

Eighteen shapes ship in the box: clover, flower, triangle, square, blob, ghost, circle, drop, star, droid, mech, alien, hexagon, cat, cloud, pill, pebble and puddle. The studio shows them all and writes the markup for you.

From JavaScript#

createBot() puts an avatar in any element (or a selector) and hands back a controller:

import { createBot } from '@kucukkanat/bots';

const bot = createBot('#agent', { type: 'droid', size: 96, glasses: 'round' });

bot.setState('thinking');   // while your agent works
bot.set({ hat: 'crown' });  // change anything, it eases in
bot.poke();                 // hop and turn round
bot.destroy();              // remove it and free its canvas

The element exposes the same controller as el.bot, and forwards the common methods (el.poke(), el.react(), el.lookAt()…).

Agent states#

States are how the avatar tells people what your agent is doing. Switch them as your agent moves through a turn:

StateLooks likeUse it when
defaultidle: looks around, blinks, the odd hopnothing is happening
listeningleans in, smiles, nods now and thenthe user is typing or talking
thinkingeyes up and aside, a thought bubblethe model is working on a reply
speakingmouth movesthe reply is streaming or being read out
workingbusy bouncinga tool call or long task is running
successa happy hopthe task finished
errorfrowns, shakes its headsomething failed
sleepingeyes closed, Z'sidle for a while

For a full turn wired to a streaming model, see Agent recipes.
